data:
Status: planned (wave 2). There is no repository and no code yet, and hull is a working name. These pages describe the plan, not a release.
Convex hulls, Delaunay triangulations, Voronoi diagrams and alpha shapes.
data.depends-on#Depends on: predicates, and go-ndarray for the array facade.
data.how-it-will-be-validated#How it will be: Combinatorial validity: the Euler relation, and the empty-circumsphere test with exact predicates. The vertex set equals the oracle’s up to degeneracies; the number of differing simplices is reported only for cocircular input, where non-uniqueness is legitimate.
data.reference-implementations-and-licences#R:
What exists, under which licence, and what that allows:
Implementation Licence and use SciPy spatial BSD-3-Clause; the oracle for hulls, Delaunay and Voronoi (it wraps Qhull) Qhull custom licence with five conditions, not an SPDX one: an oracle until those conditions are read Octave delaunay, convhull an oracle that mirrors MATLAB semantics CGAL GPL-3.0+ or LGPL-3.0+: an oracle only GPL, LGPL, AGPL and non-free code is never ported: it is only run as an oracle, as an external program.
data.references#References:
The algorithms and the theory the package will start from, as the roadmap’s bibliography lists them:
Reference Cite Barber, Dobkin, Huhdanpaa, The Quickhull algorithm for convex hulls, ACM TOMS 22(4):469-483, 1996 doi:10.1145/235815.235821 Guibas, Stolfi, Primitives for the manipulation of general subdivisions and the computation of Voronoi diagrams, ACM TOG 4(2):74-123, 1985 doi:10.1145/282918.282923 Fortune, A sweepline algorithm for Voronoi diagrams, Algorithmica 2:153-174, 1987 doi:10.1007/BF01840357 Edelsbrunner, Mücke, Three-dimensional alpha shapes, ACM TOG 13(1):43-72, 1994 doi:10.1145/174462.156635
data.what-it-will-provide#What it will provid: convex hull 2D, 3D and n-dimensional (Quickhull, with merged facets for degenerate input) Delaunay 2D and 3D triangulations Voronoi as the dual of the Delaunay triangulation alpha shapes a filtration of the Delaunay triangulation
data.where-the-plan-lives#Where the plan live: PLAN.md, STATUS.md and the bibliography in the go-scikit roadmap.

data:
Status: planned (wave 3). There is no repository and no code yet, and meshgen is a working name. These pages describe the plan, not a release.
Constrained Delaunay triangulation and quality mesh generation, 2D then 3D.
data.depends-on#Depends on: hull and predicates. go-fem consumes the meshes.
data.how-it-will-be-validated#How it will be: Mesh quality: minimum angle, maximum aspect ratio and area conservation, reported as distributions and not only as a minimum. A mesh is never compared with an oracle’s node by node.
data.reference-implementations-and-licences#R:
What exists, under which licence, and what that allows:
Implementation Licence and use Triangle 1.6 not free for commercial use: an oracle only, built locally and never vendored TetGen 1.5 AGPL-3.0-or-later or commercial: an oracle only Gmsh GPL-2.0-or-later with a linking exception: an oracle, run as an external binary GPL, LGPL, AGPL and non-free code is never ported: it is only run as an oracle, as an external program.
data.references#References:
The algorithms and the theory the package will start from, as the roadmap’s bibliography lists them:
Reference Cite Ruppert, A Delaunay refinement algorithm for quality 2-dimensional mesh generation, J. Algorithms 18(3):548-585, 1995 doi:10.1006/jagm.1995.1021 Shewchuk, Delaunay refinement algorithms for triangular mesh generation, Comput. Geom. 22:21-74, 2002 doi:10.1016/S0925-7721(01)00047-5 Si, TetGen, a Delaunay-based quality tetrahedral mesh generator, ACM TOMS 41(2):11, 2015 doi:10.1145/2629697 Geuzaine, Remacle, Gmsh, IJNME 79(11):1309-1331, 2009 doi:10.1002/nme.2579
data.what-it-will-provide#What it will provid: 2D constrained Delaunay triangulation with Ruppert/Chew refinement and a minimum-angle guarantee 3D constrained Delaunay tetrahedralisation with refinement, after the 2D work

Status: planned (wave 2). There is no repository and no code yet, and nearest is a working name. These pages describe the plan, not a release.
k-d trees and exact nearest-neighbour search.
data.how-it-will-be-validated#How it will be: Index sets exactly equal to a brute-force search, ties broken by index, and to the oracle’s.

Implementation Licence and use gonum/gonum spatial/kdtree and vptree BSD-3-Clause; to be adopted behind the facade, not rewritten (https://github.com/gonum/gonum) SciPy cKDTree BSD-3-Clause; the oracle GPL, LGPL, AGPL and non-free code is never ported: it is only run as an oracle, as an external program.

The algorithms and the theory the package will start from, as the roadmap’s bibliography lists them:
Reference Cite Bentley, Multidimensional binary search trees used for associative searching, CACM 18(9):509-517, 1975 doi:10.1145/361002.361007
data.what-it-will-provide#What it will provid: search exact nearest neighbours and k nearest neighbours in low dimension facade a MATLAB-style knnsearch API over go-ndarray

data:
Status: planned (wave 2). There is no repository and no code yet, and predicates is a working name. These pages describe the plan, not a release.
Exact geometric predicates at near floating-point cost.
data.depends-on#Depends on: nothing. Every other package of the organization depends on it.
data.how-it-will-be-validated#How it will be: The sign of each predicate equals the sign computed with big.Rat arithmetic on random and near-degenerate input; zero mismatches. Degenerate families (cocircular grids, collinear sets) are generated in the repository.
data.reference-implementations-and-licences#R:
What exists, under which licence, and what that allows:
Implementation Licence and use Shewchuk’s predicates.c public domain; may be ported (https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~quake/robust.html) GPL, LGPL, AGPL and non-free code is never ported: it is only run as an oracle, as an external program.
data.references#References:
The algorithms and the theory the package will start from, as the roadmap’s bibliography lists them:
Reference Cite Shewchuk, Adaptive Precision Floating-Point Arithmetic and Fast Robust Geometric Predicates, Discrete Comput. Geom. 18:305-363, 1997 doi:10.1007/PL00009321
data.what-it-will-provide#What it will provid: 2D Orient2D, InCircle 3D Orient3D, InSphere method adaptive precision: a floating-point filter first, exact expansion arithmetic only when the filter cannot decide the sign
